facts.text: Hope PACE is a separate, conditional coverage path for Collier residents. CMS’s October 2026 directory lists Hope PACE under contract H5934, and Florida AHCA’s August 2026 report lists its Collier service area as operational. This is not an extra benefit added to a Medicare Advantage plan.

anchors: HOPE HOSPICE AND COMMUNITY SERVICES, INC.

facts.text: PACE requires age 55 or older, residence in the organization’s service area, a state-certified need for nursing-home-level care, and the ability to live safely in the community with PACE’s help. Hope PACE lists Charlotte, Collier and Lee counties. A ZIP match or a diagnosis alone does not establish eligibility; Hope PACE and the state must assess the individual.

PACE costs depend on coverage. Medicaid participants do not pay a monthly PACE premium. People with Medicare only or private-pay coverage need an individual premium estimate. Cost-sharing protections apply to care approved by the PACE team; unauthorized or out-of-program services can leave the participant responsible for costs.

facts.text: PACE provides its participants’ prescription coverage. Medicare.gov says joining a separate Medicare drug plan while enrolled in PACE causes disenrollment from PACE. Review existing health and drug coverage with the enrollment team before making changes.

To ask about Hope PACE, call 239-985-6400 or 866-659-7223. Ask the enrollment specialist to confirm the home address is in the service area and explain the assessment and costs. The Naples center is at 13020 Livingston Road, Suite 3, Naples, FL 34105.

For Medicare counseling, contact Florida SHINE at 1-800-963-5337 (TTY 1-800-955-8770), or use its official counseling request page. Ask for a Collier County appointment. SHINE can help review coverage choices and unresolved questions; exact provider participation still needs confirmation with the plan and provider.

anchors: connect you with a SHINE Counselor

facts.text: The official Collier SHINE directory lists counseling by appointment at Alzheimer’s Support Network, 1421 Pine Ridge Road, Naples: call 239-262-8388. It also lists Baker Senior Center Naples, 6200 Autumn Oaks Lane, for members only; call 866-413-5337 to request counseling. Dates vary, so confirm the appointment before going.

Before adding or changing Medicare coverage alongside employer or union retiree coverage, ask the benefits administrator how medical and drug benefits coordinate. Joining Medicare drug coverage can affect retiree coverage for the person, spouse or dependents. Check whether the current drug coverage is creditable and whether dropped benefits can be restored; this app has not verified the employer’s rules.

VA health benefits and Medicare have different payment and access rules. VA does not bill Medicare for care at a VA facility. VA drug coverage is creditable, but VA coverage does not automatically establish TRICARE For Life eligibility. Check the existing VA benefit and access to non-VA care before changing Medicare coverage.

anchors: If you have VA healthcare but not TRICARE

facts.text: TRICARE For Life requires confirmation of TRICARE eligibility and Medicare Part A and Part B. In most cases, a person eligible for TRICARE and Medicare Part A needs Part B to keep TRICARE. Part D is not required for TRICARE prescription coverage. Confirm the person’s benefit and coordination rules with TRICARE before changing coverage; this app does not determine eligibility.

You aren’t required to have Medicare Part D

facts.text: An older Medigap policy may include benefits that are no longer sold. Medicare’s Medigap guide says a canceled older policy cannot be recovered. Some older policies include prescription benefits; review those benefits, creditable coverage and replacement rights with the insurer and SHINE before dropping a policy or adding Part D. No replacement coverage or acceptance has been established here.

anchors: Once you cancel your old policy
